curriculum_gaps_should_add.rationale: Cited implicitly when proving the ELBO is a lower bound on log evidence and when justifying KL >= 0; a one-paragraph derivation in Appendix A would let the rest of the book reference it.

The book uses REINFORCE-style policy gradients (RLHF, PPO, GRPO) but does not show the identity grad log p(x) = (1/p(x)) grad p(x) that makes the score-function estimator unbiased. A boxed derivation in 18.1 or Appendix A would tighten the alignment chapters.

notes: Inventory grew from 252 (cycle 10) to 500 named techniques after deep h2/h3/h4/dt/caption/bibliography discovery and tightened blocklist.
Tier A (core, must-have-all-4-dimensions) settled at 75 techniques after demoting infrastructure/catalog/vendor items that surfaced as A by frequency alone.
Tier B (variants, production patterns, important models) at 189 techniques and Tier C (catalog: models, benchmarks, datasets, tools, vendors) at 236.

After surgical enrichment, file-level Tier A failures dropped from 18 to 2. The remaining two are LoRA and QLoRA, both of which actually have the missing figure in their real canonical chapter (17.1); the audit selector picks the wrong canonical (19.9 tools-of-the-trade) and would need a chapter-aware fix to credit them.
Zero Tier C orphans: every catalogued benchmark/model/tool/vendor in the inventory is mentioned at least once in the book.

Only two curriculum primitives flagged as truly absent: Jensen's inequality and the log-derivative trick. Both are low-priority since the surrounding material can be followed without them; suggested locations are listed for the next author pass.
This cycle was deliberately surgical: 11 techniques received 13 new dimensions across 10 files, rather than blanket enrichment that would dilute the existing pedagogy.
